residual: P2: A comment page whose `total` key is absent or null silently truncates the sweep to the first page: `int(page.get("total") or 0)` collapses to 0, `len(comments) >= 0` is always true, and the function returns after one request with no signal. Verified: a page `{'startAt':0,'maxResults':100,'comments':[...]}` with no `total` returns after exactly 1 call. This is the same class of shape change the line above deliberately raises on -- the docstring says 'swallowing a shape change here would silently defeat dedupe on a chatty card' -- so the missing-`total` case is the one asymmetry in an otherwise fail-closed sweep. Relatedly, a non-numeric `total` ('many') raises an unmapped ValueError rather than a JiraError.

P2: The ADF renderer and the comment normalizer assume every node and every content item is a dict carrying string text; malformed shapes raise unmapped AttributeError/TypeError that escape the JiraError contract and reach the user as a traceback instead of the {"ok": false, ...} stderr object. Verified against the module: a non-dict child in `content` -> AttributeError 'str' object has no attribute 'get'; `content` that is not a list -> AttributeError; `{'type':'text','text':None}` -> TypeError in the join; a mention whose attrs.text is null -> AttributeError on .startswith; a heading with a string `level` -> TypeError on '#' * level; and a non-dict entry in a comment page -> AttributeError at `c.get("id")`. This is inconsistent with the isinstance guards the implementer deliberately added at find_ac_field_id (a non-object catalogue entry is skipped) and resolve_acceptance_criteria (a non-str/dict field degrades) for exactly this failure mode. Trigger requires a malformed body from the server, so likelihood is low, but the blast radius is the module's public error contract that the command slice consumes.

P3: `raw.decode("utf-8")` sits inside find_ac_field_id's try block but the handler catches only JiraError, so a non-UTF-8 response body raises UnicodeDecodeError and defeats the one degrade-to-None contract this function exists to provide -- the best-effort catalogue read becomes a hard failure of the whole resolve. fetch_issue (line 331) and fetch_comments (line 406) decode the same way, where the failure mode is an unmapped traceback instead of a JiraError. Theoretical for Jira Cloud (UTF-8 JSON by spec) and already flagged by the implementer; noted here as the same unmapped-exception class as J1-R1-04.

P3: The clock-read guard is a whole-source substring scan for the literal 'datetime' with only '# ' stripped, so it constrains prose as well as code: any future docstring or comment sentence containing the word 'datetime' turns CI red for a module that still reads no clock. It has already forced one docstring rewording during this slice (per the implementer's own deviation note), which is the guard shaping the prose rather than the behaviour it means to pin.

P2: main()'s refusal output diverges from the exact two-file precedent conventions.md cites for this behavior (dag.py:775-782, run_state.py:1289-1295): both JiraUsageError (exit 2) and JiraError (exit 1) print the same JSON `{"ok": false, "errors": [...]}` shape to stderr, whereas the established repo pattern prints the contract-failure (exit 1) JSON refusal to STDOUT and the usage-failure (exit 2) message as plain `"error: %s"` text to STDERR. This is a real, verifiable output-shape/stream inconsistency with the only two files conventions.md names as the reference for this exact behavior, not a stylistic taste call -- any downstream tooling that follows the established repo idiom to distinguish the two refusal shapes/streams will not find what it expects from this module.

P2: ISSUE_KEY_RE (and ALLOWED_HOST_RE) are anchored with a bare `$` and checked with `.match()`, not `.fullmatch()`/`\Z`. In Python, `$` (without re.MULTILINE) matches at end-of-string OR just before a single trailing newline, so a key with a trailing `
` passes validation silently. Verified empirically in the worktree: `jc.validate_issue_key("ABC-123
")` returns `"ABC-123
"` unchanged instead of raising `JiraUsageError`. This contradicts both the plan's binding constraint ("Validate the Jira issue key against a strict regex ... before it reaches a URL segment, a filesystem path, or argv") and the function's own docstring claim ("Rejects ... anything else outside ISSUE_KEY_RE"). Current call sites happen to percent-encode the key before every URL use, bounding today's exploitability, but the validator's own contract is broken, and a future consumer (e.g. the deferred write-back/comment-POST slice) that trusts "already regex-validated" without re-encoding would inherit the gap. No test in the otherwise-thorough injection-negative suite (leading dash, embedded slash, path traversal) covers a trailing/embedded newline.

P3: Task 7's own instruction says to "Re-wrap the list lines to stay under the file's existing wrap width" when inserting `jira_client` into the Scripts enumeration, but the resulting third line of the bullet is 84 characters wide, longer than every other line in the same Components bullet block (the surrounding Agents/Skills/Scripts lines all sit at 55-78 chars) -- it was not re-wrapped, it was left to grow.

deferred: PREMISE / forward risk for the command slice, NOT to be built here: this module renders untrusted Jira prose into MARKDOWN (headings as `## X`, lists as `- `, fenced code blocks) and hands it to a downstream consumer that will feed it to a model. Card text containing `## Acceptance Criteria` or instruction-shaped prose becomes structurally indistinguishable from the intake command's own prose. Two consequences: (a) `acceptance_criteria_from_description` can be steered by attacker-authored heading text; (b) the command slice's untrusted-data framing (peer-review.md:48-51) must fence or delimit `description`/`acceptance_criteria`/comment bodies rather than inline them. Log this for the command slice; do not expand j1's record contract to carry it.

Untrusted card text reaches a human reviewer and an agent unfiltered for invisible Unicode. `adf_to_text` (Task 3) renders summary, description and every comment body verbatim, and `main` emits them with `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)` (Task 6, j1.md:1368). JSON escapes C0 controls but not Unicode bidi and format characters (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069, U+200B-200F), so card text can render one way for a human reading the artifact and another for the model consuming it -- a Trojan-Source-shaped trick on a field the run already designates untrusted. The boundary where this is enforced belongs to the command slice per the run's own framing, so out of scope here, but `adf_to_text` is the natural single home for a strip and this should not be lost between slices. Mitigation when it is taken up: strip category-Cf characters in the renderer, with a test asserting a U+202E-bearing comment body round-trips clean.
